drafted_from: tool:prepare-a-server-for-a-door-tunnel's row in keep-a-door-tunnel-open/tool-rows.json, do-work/keep-a-door-tunnel-open.mjs, do-work/prepare-a-tunnel-host.sh and test/keep-a-door-tunnel-open.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Set up my rented server at 192.0.2.34 so the user tunnel-user can hold a tunnel from its port 18789 back to my door on port 8789 and do nothing else." It runs tool:prepare-a-server-for-a-door-tunnel with your server's host key and the public half of the tunnel's key, and tells you whether the server was prepared.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it takes its server details as input and changes the server over SSH.
instructions: 1. Hold your server administration key under the name server-administration-ssh-key (the door mounts it for the run); make a tunnel key pair and keep its private half in your vault. You need the server's IPv4 address, SSH port, administrator user and host key ("<type> <base64>").

2. Say "Set up my server to hold a door tunnel" and give your AI the address, ssh_port, admin_user, host_key, the service user, remotePort (the server's loopback port), localPort (your door's port) and publicKey (the tunnel key's public half).
3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:prepare-a-server-for-a-door-tunnel and that input (the worked example shows one).

4. Read what comes back: {"prepared": true, "said": "tunnel-host-prepared: <user> may listen only on 127.0.0.1:<remotePort>"}. Keeping the tunnel open afterwards is a launch agent that runs serve on your computer; it is not part of this tool.

worked_examples.title: Prepare a server so tunnel-user may listen only on 127.0.0.1:18789
worked_examples.ask: Set up my server at 192.0.2.34 so tunnel-user can hold a tunnel to my door and nothing else.
worked_examples.given: From tools/keep-a-door-tunnel-open/test/keep-a-door-tunnel-open.test.mjs (the prepareFromRequest case, which stubs the SSH call; no real server was reached) with the same request. The run pins the host key as "[192.0.2.34]:2222 <host_key>", signs in as admin@192.0.2.34 through the run's proxy, runs do-work/prepare-a-tunnel-host.sh (which writes the restricted authorized_keys line and the sshd Match block, checks sshd -t, reloads ssh and prints its last line), and answers with that last line, read from the code.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"prepared": true, "said": "tunnel-host-prepared: tunnel-user may listen only on 127.0.0.1:18789"}. A request without host_key is refused with an error that says host_key is missing.
